open_questions: Phase-curve amplitude (3086 ppm, ratio_to_depth 1.108) is larger than transit depth and star_density_penalty 256.1 explains 6709% of fit chi2, indicating large undiluted spot modulation at 1.18 d (rotation amplitude 12455-21524 ppm) - RV and high-precision photometry needed to measure radius/mass and confirm transit is not spot-shaped.

xgboost planet_rank 0.23 is low for a real planet; follow-up should weigh against theoretical maximum planet size for 0.2126 M_sun M dwarf and test for spot harmonics (sector 60 shows 0.587 d, half-period alias).

Duration ratio 1.591 (TIC) to 1.471 (Gaia FLAME) and large star_density_penalty suggest shallow impact parameter / evolved radius; precise stellar radius from spectroscopy would refine rp_rearth 1.395 vs 1.51 and rule out grazing VB.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 0.28% flat, on-target dip every 1.18 days (85 events, SNR ~14) on a nearby 0.24 solar-radius M dwarf, with no odd/even difference or strong secondary and no neighbour able to cause the dip. The depth implies a 1.4 Earth-size planet, the best explanation despite a large brightness swing at the same period from the star's own starspots. A 1.1 Earth-size radius star can still plausibly host such a signal, so precise follow-up of the variability is needed to confirm.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target and rules out neighbours that could fake it; positively favours an on-target transit over a blended binary.
reasons.value: on_target (offset_arcsec 2.679, offset_sigma 0.8757, suspects 17.6-23.4 sigma away, plausible_within_1px 0, could_cause_within_1px 0)

reasons.why: Flat-bottomed, no odd/even depth difference (depth_odd_ppm 2800 vs depth_even_ppm 2518, ratio 1.1) and no significant secondary (secondary.snr 2.919, best_brightening_snr 7.972); favours planet over grazing/eclipsing binary despite xgboost planet_rank 0.23.

Planet-sized dip on a 0.242 R_sun (TIC) / 0.263 R_sun (Gaia FLAME) M dwarf with high-SNR, steady sector depths (sectors.p_constant 0.2333) and duration ratio 1.59 (stellar density penalty 256.1 noted) is best explained as a planet, even on a spotted star.
reasons.value: 1.395 (undiluted_depth_ppm 2787, rp_over_rstar 0.05279) with 85 transits, refit snr 14.18, share 0.0456

reasons.why: Period coincides with rotation, but young active M dwarf (phot_variable_flag VARIABLE, 17594-21524 ppm variability) commonly shows 1:1 chance alignment; large phase-curve swing and star_density_penalty are against a planet but are blemishes, not positive evidence for an alternative, and similar returns are 5/5 planet confirmations, supporting gate2.
reasons.value: signal_period_d 1.1778 vs rotation_d 1.178, signal_over_rotation 0.999830220713073, phase_curve.amplitude_ppm 3086 ratio_to_depth 1.108 chi2 200.1 dof 9
